stories.label: Alarm and scepticism follow Trump's Kharg Island threat
stories.summary: Trump says the US will be 'taking Kharg Island' — the terminal that handles roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports — and other oil infrastructure. Lead with the escalation the threat represents: seizing a named country's primary export node is an act of war and economic strangulation in one, not a market headline. The structural why is how the US is reframing a chokepoint conflict from interdiction to outright capture of sovereign energy assets, and why analysts are sceptical it is operationally real. Multi-source with regional voices (Al Jazeera QA, Dawn PK) alongside US/Indian wires. Lead from the verified threat, flag the scepticism, do not present seizure as accomplished.

stories.label: World Bank revises global growth forecast down over Iran war impact
stories.summary: The World Bank cut its global growth forecast to the lowest since the pandemic and labelled the 2020s a 'lost decade' for developing countries — pinning the latest downgrade on the US-Iran war and its Hormuz spillover. Lead with who bears it: developing economies, already battered by serial shocks, facing higher fertiliser, fuel and food costs from a war they have no part in. The structural why is how a single regional conflict transmits through energy and shipping into a worldwide growth penalty concentrated on the poorest. Regional source (TRT World, TR) anchors the multi-source pair.

stories.label: Dozens killed in drone attacks across Sudan as El Obeid toll reaches 23
stories.summary: Drone strikes across Sudan killed at least 30 civilians and five soldiers this week, with El Obeid in North Kordofan worst hit (23 civilian dead). Lead with the named victims and the mechanism: cheap one-way drones are turning Sudan's war into a campaign of remote civilian killing far from any front line. The structural why is how a conflict the world has stopped watching keeps killing at scale, documented here by a Sudanese outlet (Radio Dabanga) when Western wires are absent. Dignity and consequence; directly addresses the audit's Africa coverage gap.

stories.label: Bangladesh's Myanmar Border Challenge Is No Longer Just About the Rohingya
stories.summary: Bangladeshis are being abducted and killed by the Arakan Army, the de facto power across the border in Myanmar's Rakhine — but Dhaka has no official channel to a non-state actor it cannot recognise. Lead with that diplomatic trap: a sovereign state unable to protect its own citizens because the authority on the other side of the line is not a government. The structural why is how the collapse of the Myanmar state has handed border control to armed groups, rewriting what 'foreign relations' even means for neighbours. Asia hard-news pick; OIC-member Bangladesh, no regional Bangladeshi outlet in feed — note for feed-side audit.

stories.label: India evacuates crew after tanker fire off Oman
stories.summary: The asphalt tanker Jalveer is ablaze off Oman and its crew evacuated, the latest civilian shipping casualty as the US-Iran war reaches into the Gulf of Oman approaches to Hormuz — Indian sailors are among the dead in the wider strikes. Lead with the human and commercial cost converging on one waterway: crews killed, hulls burning, and the insurance-and-freight shock that radiates from every hit. The structural why is how a chokepoint war turns neutral merchant shipping into collateral, raising the cost of every barrel and container that transits. Multi-source (Middle East Eye, Al Jazeera QA, RT RU).

stories.label: SpaceX IPO Could Test Market, Says 1789 Capital's Abrahimzadeh
stories.summary: SpaceX's public debut is shaping up as the year's stress test for investor appetite, with BlackRock alone reportedly seeking at least $5bn of shares. Lead with the concentration the IPO reveals: a single privately-held launch-and-satellite monopoly is about to absorb a record slug of institutional capital just as Nvidia slips toward bear territory and AI names sell off. The structural why is how much of the market's risk budget is now bet on one founder's rocket-and-Starlink complex — and what a wobble would mean. Multi-source (Bloomberg, Investing.com IN, Yahoo Finance).

stories.label: Vietnam enacts first halal law to boost exports and Muslim tourism
stories.summary: Vietnam has passed its first national halal law — a non-Muslim-majority state legislating to certify exports and court Muslim travellers. Lead with the strategic read: Hanoi is treating the $2-trillion-plus global halal economy as an export lane and tourism market to be captured, not a faith matter. The structural why is how the halal standard has become trade infrastructure — and how Southeast Asian exporters are racing to meet OIC-market certification rather than cede ground to Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. Reader-aligned Muslim-world economy pick from a specialist outlet (Salaam Gateway).

stories.label: S&P Global flags food prices as potential driver of inflation across emerging markets
stories.summary: S&P Global warns food costs may overtake energy as the chief inflation driver across emerging markets, with African economies likely hit hardest as fertiliser and transport costs climb. Lead with the distributional sting: in economies where households already spend most of their income on food, a few percentage points is hunger, not a CPI line. The structural why is how the same war-driven fuel and fertiliser shock that the World Bank flagged converts into bread-and-staple inflation precisely where buffers are thinnest. Regional source (Premium Times, NG); reinforces the Africa coverage gap.

stories.label: Amazon deforestation is falling, but progress is stalling
stories.summary: Brazil cleared 984,794 hectares of native vegetation in 2025 — below a million for the first time since 2019, a 20.6% drop on 2024 — but the rate of improvement is flattening. Lead with the concrete numbers and the plateau they reveal: enforcement gains hit a ceiling once the easy reductions are banked. The structural why is that headline deforestation declines mask a stalling trend, and a stalled Amazon is still a net carbon and biodiversity loss. Reader-aligned Global South environmental science with a measurable mechanism.

stories.label: How Tuvalu Is Rewriting the Rules of Statehood
stories.summary: As rising seas threaten to submerge its land, Tuvalu is pioneering a legal doctrine that a state's sovereignty survives even if its territory does not. Lead with the precedent it sets: a nation pre-emptively rewriting international law so statehood, maritime zones and citizenship persist for a 'digital' or deterritorialised country. The structural why is that climate change is forcing a redefinition of one of the oldest concepts in the state system — and small Pacific nations, not great powers, are authoring it. Fills the persistent Oceania coverage gap flagged in the audit.

stories.label: Amazon Data Centers In Mississippi Have Already Raised Electricity Rates for Local Customers, Report Suggests
stories.summary: Three Amazon data centers in Mississippi aren't even open yet, but a new study finds local residents already pay at least $10.60 more a month to subsidise them. Lead with that number and who pays it: ordinary ratepayers underwriting hyperscale AI infrastructure before a single server boots. The structural why is how utility rate design quietly socialises the grid costs of the AI boom onto households while the compute benefits accrue to a trillion-dollar company. Reader-aligned accountability reporting from 404 Media on the hidden local economics of the data-center buildout.

stories.label: Flock Leaked Cops' License Plate Searches via DuckDuckGo, Bing
stories.summary: Flock, the automatic license-plate-reader firm, exposed which plates police were hunting and why — leaking the searches through ordinary search engines like DuckDuckGo and Bing. Lead with the irony of the surveillance machine surveilling itself into the open: the queries reveal the reasons cops ran searches, an audit trail no one was supposed to see. The structural why is how a sprawling private ALPR network accumulates sensitive policing data with so little security that a misconfiguration spills it to the public web. Reader-aligned privacy exposé from an original-reporting outlet (404 Media).

stories.label: Big banks are ditching private blockchains to build tokenized cash networks on public infrastructure
stories.summary: European banks are abandoning the walled-garden private ledgers they spent a decade building and moving tokenized cash onto public blockchains instead. Lead with the reversal: the institutions that dismissed public chains as unfit for finance are now standardising on them, sidelining policymakers' preference for central-bank-led digital money. The structural why is that bank-backed tokenized deposits, not euro stablecoins or CBDCs, may become the rails for institutional money — a quiet contest over who controls the next payment layer. Reader-aligned fintech-infrastructure story (CoinDesk).

stories.label: Britain's defence ⁠minister Healey quits over defence spending
stories.summary: Defence Secretary John Healey resigned, telling Starmer the UK's investment plan 'falls well short of what is required... at this dangerous time.' Lead with the fracture this exposes: a cabinet minister quitting over too little military spending — at the exact moment a Gulf war is driving up energy and security costs — signals a Treasury-versus-defence rupture inside Labour. The structural why is how the Hormuz/Iran shock is now reshaping European fiscal politics, forcing rearmament debates that split governing parties. Only genuine multi-source event in today's feed (UK, US, Qatar, India, HK wires).

stories.label: Violence in Mogadishu, a fractured elite: What renewed violence means for Somalia and its backers
stories.summary: Renewed armed clashes in Mogadishu trace not to al-Shabaab but to a fracturing of Somalia's own political elite — and to the foreign backers (Gulf states, Turkey, the US) who arm rival factions. Lead with the agency reversal: this is a contest among Somali power-holders, not a Western counterterror footnote. The structural why is how external patronage hardens internal splits in a state already managing famine and displacement. Regional outlet (Mada Masr, EG) on an under-covered Horn of Africa story; addresses the day's Africa coverage gap.

stories.label: India 'actively working' to deprive Pakistan of water
stories.summary: India's water minister says 'not a single drop' will flow to Pakistan after New Delhi put the Indus Waters Treaty into abeyance following the 2025 Pahalgam attack. Lead with the weaponization of water: a 65-year treaty that survived three wars is now being used as leverage against 240 million downstream Pakistanis who depend on the Indus for agriculture and drinking water. The structural why is how a stated policy of denial converts a shared river into an instrument of coercion. Regional source (Dawn, PK); named-victim geography the reader tracks.

stories.label: 'A Nakba of 2026': An IDF reservist recounts his time in Lebanon
stories.summary: An identity-verified IDF reservist describes orders to flatten the southern Lebanese village of Aitaroun — satellite imagery confirms near-total destruction — where a hunting rifle plus a Hezbollah flag was enough to mark a home 'terrorist infrastructure.' Lead with the mechanism of collective punishment: how a deliberately loose definition converts an entire town into a demolition target. The structural why is the documented pattern — corroborated by Haaretz, +972 and Breaking the Silence — of revenge-driven, indiscriminate razing. Dignity and named-victim framing; first-person accountability testimony, not an unsourced claim.

stories.label: Philippine Foreign Secretary Says She Will Meet Myanmar Opposition Groups Soon
stories.summary: Manila's foreign secretary will meet Myanmar opposition groups even as ASEAN states move to normalize ties with the junta's new 'civilian' government in Naypyidaw. Lead with the split inside ASEAN: one member reaching past the generals to the resistance while the bloc as a whole rehabilitates a coup regime. The structural why is how a 'civilian' relabeling launders military rule into diplomatic legitimacy — and whether engagement with the opposition can survive that consensus. Accountability angle on regional complicity.

stories.label: Bangladesh Targets Growth Revival With Record Budget Spending
stories.summary: Bangladesh's post-Hasina government unveiled its first budget — record spending aimed at 6.5% growth and 7.5% inflation, financed partly by automating and flattening tax collection. Lead with the political-economy stakes: a transitional government betting that fiscal expansion and a simplified tax can revive a garment-export economy battered by a year of upheaval. The structural why is whether a fragile new administration can widen a notoriously thin tax base without reigniting unrest. Major OIC-economy story; feed carried no Bangladeshi regional outlet — note for feed-side audit.

stories.label: Is Trump finally burying the zombie US-Mexico-Canada trade pact?
stories.summary: Trump confirmed he won't reauthorize USMCA before the June 30 deadline, triggering a decade of annual reviews. Lead with the confirmed fact, then the asymmetry: Washington wants rules-of-origin rewritten to force more content into the US (raising USMCA-wide minimums to 82% and US-specific content to 50%) — favorable to Mexico's assembly base, punishing to high-wage Canada. The structural why is how 'free trade' is being re-engineered into managed reshoring, with Canada the designated loser amid a sovereignty feud. Trade-mechanism story the reader will grasp; lead from the verified non-renewal, not the analysis.

stories.label: A Leap of Faith: Inside Syria's First Frog Farm
stories.summary: In Hama's Sahl al-Ghab, a returnee who learned the trade while displaced in Turkey has built Syria's first frog farm, betting an abundant wild population can anchor a new export industry less than a year after Assad's fall. Lead with the micro-economics of return: a single entrepreneur testing whether post-war Syria can build legal export value chains from scratch. The structural why is what reconstruction actually looks like at ground level — skills carried home by the displaced, seeding industries the old regime never allowed. OIC-region economic texture; geographic-diversity pick.

stories.label: On the hunt for cosmic dawn and the universe's very first stars
stories.summary: JWST and cosmologists like UCL's Richard Ellis have pushed the observable 'lookback' horizon to the era of the universe's very first stars and galaxies — 'cosmic dawn,' once theoretical, is now within reach of a four-year-old telescope. Lead with the threshold crossed: we are observing light from when the first luminous objects switched on. The structural why is how a single instrument compresses the gap between cosmological theory and direct observation, letting us test models of how structure first formed. Reader-aligned wonder with a concrete mechanism.

stories.label: 'We still need people to hold our hands': Inside the collapse of Malawi's humanitarian safety net
stories.summary: As 'climate whiplash' — drought then flood — collides with a shrinking global aid budget, Malawi's humanitarian safety net is unraveling and the people it caught are exposed. Lead with the compound failure: climate shocks intensifying exactly as the donor funding that once buffered them is withdrawn. The structural why is how aid retrenchment in Western capitals transmits directly into food insecurity for the world's poorest, who did least to cause the warming now hitting them. Named-victim, accountability framing; addresses the Africa coverage gap.

stories.label: China builds a rival satellite constellation as SpaceX goes public
stories.summary: A Chinese state-backed firm (SpaceSail) is signing up the governments and partners Starlink has shut out — days before SpaceX's record IPO. Lead with the bifurcation: low-earth-orbit internet is splitting into US and Chinese constellations, and the Global South is being asked to pick an orbital patron. The structural why is that satellite connectivity is becoming the next infrastructure-dependency choice, with the terms of access set by two powers. Reader-aligned geopolitics-of-tech story; non-Western agency angle.

stories.label: FCC Wants to Kill Burner Phones By Forcing Telecoms to Get All Customers' IDs
stories.summary: The FCC wants to legally compel telecoms to collect every new and renewing customer's government ID number and physical address — ending anonymous prepaid phones. Lead with who loses anonymity: not just the privacy-conscious, but domestic-abuse survivors and others for whom an untraceable phone is a safety tool. The structural why is how an anti-fraud framing quietly builds a nationwide identity-to-device registry, a surveillance capability that outlives its stated purpose. Reader-aligned privacy/accountability exposé from an original-reporting outlet.

stories.label: Google DeepMind is worried about what happens when millions of agents start to interact
stories.summary: Google DeepMind is funding research into the risks of millions of autonomous AI agents interacting online — a hazard class its own AGI-safety director says is barely studied. Lead with the admission: the firm racing to deploy agents is also conceding it can't predict their collective behavior. The structural why is that emergent dynamics — collusion, cascades, manipulation — arise at the system level, not the single-model level, exactly where oversight is weakest. Reader-aligned AI story that names the accountability gap between deployment speed and safety understanding.

stories.label: IRGC closes Strait of Hormuz until further notice
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC Navy declared the Strait of Hormuz fully closed to all shipping, citing repeated US ceasefire violations, and struck two vessels that tried to run the closure. Lead with the chokepoint mechanism: roughly a fifth of the world's traded oil moves through this strait, so a declared closure is an economic act with global reach — fuel, freight, and insurance costs transmit within hours to import-dependent economies (Pakistan's austerity drive, the Pacific's fuel shock already trace to this war). The structural why is how a single waterway converts a regional war into a worldwide supply shock. Iranian state source is the regional voice here; the closure is a stated policy act even where battlefield claims are contested.

stories.label: One in 70 people worldwide is forcibly displaced: UNHCR
stories.summary: UNHCR counts 117.8 million forcibly displaced — one in 70 people alive — but reports the first decline in a decade, driven by large-scale returns to Afghanistan and Syria. Lead with the paradox: the headline number falls not because the world grew safer but because exhausted refugees are being pushed or pulled back into still-fragile countries. The structural why is that 'return' is being counted as resolution even where the conditions that caused flight persist. Names the named-victim geographies the reader tracks — Afghanistan, Syria, Sudan.

stories.label: Thailand court sentences two men to death for 2015 Bangkok bombing
stories.summary: A Thai court handed death sentences to two Uighur men for the 2015 Erawan shrine bombing that killed 20 — the country's deadliest attack. Lead with the contested backdrop: the defendants are Uighurs, and the bombing followed Thailand's forced deportation of 100+ Uighurs to China weeks earlier, making the prosecution inseparable from Beijing's transnational reach. The structural why is how a capital verdict, eleven years on, closes a case whose political origins were never fully aired. Multi-source synthesis (Qatar, Japan, UK wires diverge on framing).

stories.label: Why the Indo-Pacific Trade Hinges on East Africa
stories.summary: East Africa's ports, sea lanes and offshore gas fields have quietly become contested ground in the competition stretching from the Gulf to the Pacific. Lead with the agency reversal: this frames East African states (Tanzania, Mozambique, Kenya) not as a Western policy backdrop but as gatekeepers whose infrastructure choices shape Indo-Pacific trade. The structural why is how middle and smaller powers monetize geography — and why a chokepoint war in the Gulf (see Hormuz) makes alternative African routing strategically valuable. Geographic-diversity pick to offset the day's Gulf/Asia gravity.

stories.label: BTC, ETH, SOL price news: Bitcoin has reached a deep bear-market valuation zone
stories.summary: Bitcoin has fallen into a valuation band it has historically reached only at cycle bottoms, squeezed by hot headline inflation (4.2% annual), fading hopes of US regulatory clarity, and rising global rates ahead of the June FOMC. Lead with the macro linkage the reader will grasp: crypto, sold as an inflation hedge, is now trading like a high-beta risk asset that falls hardest exactly when inflation and geopolitical stress spike. The structural why is the collapse of the 'digital gold' thesis under real-rate pressure.

stories.label: Sustained care critical for Gaza's child amputees
stories.summary: Gaza now holds one of the world's highest per-capita concentrations of child amputees, and the medical story is not the amputation but what comes after: a growing child outgrows a prosthetic limb roughly every year, so a one-time fitting is not care — it is the start of a decade-long supply chain that the siege has severed. Lead with that mechanism. The structural why is how blockade converts a survivable injury into lifelong disability by cutting off follow-up prosthetics and physiotherapy. Dignity and named-victim framing; reader-aligned Global South science source. Feed carried no regional Palestinian outlet on this specific piece — note for feed-side audit.

stories.label: The Great AI Divide: Navigating U.S. and Chinese dominance
stories.summary: As frontier AI consolidates into a US-versus-China duopoly, the rest of the world faces a dependency choice: build on American models, Chinese models, or be locked out of both. Lead with the sovereignty stakes for the Global South — compute, language coverage, and data-governance terms are all being set by two powers, leaving smaller nations as price-takers. The structural why is that AI dependency is becoming the new infrastructure dependency, replicating older patterns of technological non-alignment. Geographic-agency angle the reader will value.

stories.label: Building an HTML-first site doubled our users overnight
stories.summary: A developer rebuilt a JavaScript-heavy web app as server-rendered HTML and reports user numbers doubling overnight — a story that resonated to the top of Hacker News (1,096 points). Lead with the measured outcome, then the mechanism: heavy client-side frameworks silently exclude users on slow networks, cheap devices, and high-latency connections — disproportionately the Global South. The structural why is that 'modern web' defaults impose an access tax, and stripping them back is both a performance and an equity decision. Reader-aligned dev story that mirrors this site's own HTML-first philosophy.

stories.label: Overnight Attacks Rattle U.S.-Iran Ceasefire (Updated)
stories.summary: The dominant thread advances: overnight tit-for-tat strikes are among the most severe since the April 8 ceasefire, with Israel's continued attacks on Lebanon (thousands killed, over a million displaced) sabotaging any de-escalation. Lead with the mechanism of a ceasefire that exists on paper while the killing continues — and the named victims in Lebanon, not just the great-power maneuvering. Continuation of the war IS the development. Follows yesterday's Hormuz-oil thread but from the ground-war angle, not Trump's logistics claim.

stories.label: The Pacific's fuel shock extracts a price from women
stories.summary: The same Middle East oil crisis driving headlines elsewhere lands on Pacific island women — measured not in shipping routes or state-of-emergency declarations but in lost income, longer unpaid labor, and reduced safety as fuel scarcity reshapes daily life. Lead with that distributional mechanism: who actually bears the cost of a chokepoint war 12,000km away. Fills the persistent Oceania coverage gap (1 article yesterday) and connects the global energy shock to the most invisible affected population.

stories.label: Collapsing like a 'mansion of cards': Divisions within the Civil Democratic Movement
stories.summary: Egypt's main civilian opposition coalition is fracturing from within — original reporting from one of the few independent newsrooms still operating under Cairo's pressure. Lead with the structural why: how an authoritarian state doesn't need to ban an opposition when internal divisions and attrition do the work for it. A rare regional voice on Egyptian politics that Western wires will not carry; protect it as a unique source.

stories.label: Property information withheld -- the Cape Town planning tribunal that answers to no-one
stories.summary: An investigative series exposes how Cape Town's land-use planning tribunal withholds property records and operates without recorded baselines — a body that approves who builds what, accountable to no one. Lead with the accountability gap as the mechanism: opacity at the municipal level is how planning capture works, with public-record requests stonewalled. Original South African investigative reporting; illuminates a structural pattern (institutional capture via information control) beyond the single city.

stories.label: Dar-led committee recommends extending countrywide austerity drive till June 30
stories.summary: Pakistan extends a nationwide austerity and fuel-conservation drive because the US-Israel-Iran war has triggered a global oil crisis — a direct domestic transmission of the chokepoint conflict into ordinary Pakistanis' lives. Lead with the causal chain: a war on Iran begun February 28 now dictates fuel rationing in Islamabad. The structural why is the fragility of an import-dependent economy exposed to a war it has no part in. Regional source (Dawn, PK) on an OIC-region story.

stories.label: Why the India-Oman CEPA is Special
stories.summary: India and Oman's trade agreement took effect June 1 — and its quiet strategic value is geography: much of Oman's coast lies outside the Strait of Hormuz, giving India a trade gateway that sidesteps the world's most contested chokepoint just as a war chokes it. Lead with that hedge against Hormuz risk as the mechanism. The structural why is how middle powers route around great-power conflict zones. Oman is an OIC member; feed carried no Gulf/regional outlet on this — note for feed-side audit.

stories.label: S.Korea hits Coupang with record fine over e-commerce data leak
stories.summary: South Korea fined Coupang — its largest online retailer, US-incorporated — a record $409M over a massive data breach that surfaced in November and became friction between Seoul and Washington. Lead with the accountability number: regulators pricing a breach at scale, against a platform that holds tens of millions of citizens' personal data. The structural why is data-sovereignty as statecraft — a national regulator forcing a US-listed company to answer for leaked personal data. Multi-source (HK/IN/US wires diverge mildly, 0.09).

stories.label: Govt may hold off on higher ethanol mandate
stories.summary: India scrapped excise duty on petrol blended up to 30% ethanol to cut reliance on imported crude — but is simultaneously delaying a higher blending mandate over engine-damage concerns. Lead with the tension: a clean-energy/import-substitution push colliding with the physical reality that older engines can't safely run high-ethanol fuel. The structural why is energy security under a war-driven oil crisis, and the limits of biofuel as a substitute. Multi-source (three Indian outlets, divergence 0.19).

stories.label: Deadly Indonesia floods wiped out at least 7% of rare orangutan population, report says
stories.summary: Cyclone-induced floods that killed at least 1,200 people and damaged 300,000 homes in Sumatra also killed 58 critically endangered Tapanuli orangutans — at least 7% of the entire remaining population of the world's rarest great ape. Lead with the dual human-and-species toll and the named cause: rapid deforestation that amplified the disaster. The structural why is how habitat destruction converts a weather event into an extinction-level blow. Indonesia is an OIC member; feed carried no regional (Jakarta Post) outlet — note for audit.

stories.label: Guest post: How a record-high 'energy imbalance' is driving global warming
stories.summary: Earth's 'energy imbalance' — the gap between incoming solar energy and outgoing heat — has hit a record high, meaning the planet is now accumulating heat faster than at any measured point. Lead with the mechanism the reader can hold onto: warming is not just emissions but the rate at which trapped energy is building, and that rate is accelerating. The structural why is that this metric, not surface temperature alone, is the truest gauge of how fast the climate system is being pushed. Reader-aligned climate-science source.

stories.label: Boeing's New Larger Ghost Bat Can Carry AIM-120 AMRAAMs Internally
stories.summary: Boeing's autonomous 'Ghost Bat' combat drone is entering a third, larger iteration that can carry air-to-air missiles internally — a step toward uncrewed aircraft that hunt and kill without a pilot. Lead with the capability shift as the mechanism: internal weapons bays mean a stealthy, expendable drone can now fight as a true combat aircraft, not just a sensor. The structural why is the economics and ethics of autonomous lethality — pushing the human further from the kill decision as drone-on-drone warfare becomes affordable at scale.

stories.label: Bill Gates testifies in closed-door US House meeting over Epstein ties
stories.summary: One of the world's richest men gave sworn closed-door testimony to the House about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, saying Epstein tried to use his extramarital affairs as leverage. Lead with the accountability mechanism: a congressional panel forcing a private philanthropist to account for proximity to a convicted sex trafficker, and what 'closed-door' conceals from the public. Power sits with Gates and the committee; the structural why is how wealth buys discretion even under subpoena. Multi-source — Qatari, British and Indian wires diverge in tone (0.34).

stories.label: Hegseth Visits Guantanamo and Warns Cuba Against Seeking Weapons
stories.summary: The US defense secretary stood on the occupied Guantanamo base — territory Cuba has never consented to lease — and warned Havana not to arm itself. Lead with that irony as the mechanism: a superpower threatening a sanctioned island from a base on the island's own soil. The structural why is the asymmetry of the embargo era, with Cuba already in fuel-and-food collapse under US pressure. Multi-source across US, UK, Singapore, India and Qatar.

stories.label: Senate panel threatens arrest warrant against Ex-NNPC MD, Mele Kyari over "missing" N210trn
stories.summary: Nigeria's Senate is moving to arrest the former head of the state oil company over a ₦210 trillion discrepancy the Auditor-General flagged across 2017-2023 accounts. Lead with the scale of the number against a country where most live on a few dollars a day. The structural why is how oil revenue vanishes inside a national champion that operates beyond audit — and whether a legislature can actually compel its own elite to answer. Original Nigerian reporting; fills the Africa coverage gap.

stories.label: Ethnic Restaurants and Immigrant Entrepreneurs Facing Crisis Under Japan's New Visa Rules
stories.summary: Japan's tightened business-manager visa rules — meant to curb abuse — are squeezing the immigrant entrepreneurs who run the country's ethnic restaurants, raising capital and staffing thresholds many small founders can't meet. Lead with the human cost: genuine small-business owners caught by a rule aimed at fraud. The structural why is how an aging, labor-short Japan simultaneously needs migrants and erects barriers against them. Fills the Asia coverage gap.

stories.label: Trump says US will attack Iran 'very hard' and has taken oil through Hormuz
stories.summary: Set aside the threat and lead with the disclosure underneath it: Trump says the US military secretly escorted ships carrying more than 100 million barrels of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz. The mechanism for the reader is energy-supply statecraft — Washington quietly moving a strategic oil volume through the world's most contested chokepoint while inflation runs at 4.2%. The structural why is how a war footing reshapes oil logistics and feeds back into US household prices. Multi-source, US/India wires.

stories.label: BlackRock and Fidelity are quietly turning bitcoin ETFs into a two-firm market
stories.summary: Bitcoin was sold as decentralized money; two years after spot ETFs launched, BlackRock and Fidelity now command the flows in a winner-take-most market that starves smaller issuers. Lead with that contradiction. The structural why for the reader is how scale, liquidity and distribution networks reassert the same concentration in crypto that defines traditional finance — the asset changed, the power structure didn't. Reader-aligned macro source.

stories.label: You Can't Bet on Little League
stories.summary: Kalshi turned itself into a nationwide sports-betting venue by reclassifying wagers as 'event contracts' under federal commodities law — sidestepping every state that banned or regulated sports gambling. Lead with the regulatory arbitrage as the mechanism: a prediction market exploiting a CFTC loophole to do legally what states forbid. The structural why is how a single federal carve-out can hollow out 50 states' gambling rules overnight, and where the line gets drawn.

stories.label: ESA Awards Initial €700M Contract for Next-Gen Sentinel-1 Satellites
stories.summary: Europe is paying €700M for two next-generation Sentinel-1 radar satellites to replace an aging fleet that watches the planet day and night through cloud. Lead with what the satellites actually do: synthetic-aperture radar tracks ice loss, oil spills, ground subsidence and flood extent regardless of weather — the unglamorous backbone of climate and disaster monitoring. The structural why is sovereignty over Earth observation, and the continuity risk when only three of the original four satellites still fly.

stories.label: Melanesian nations vow to connect and expand marine protected areas
stories.summary: Melanesian states are pledging to link and expand marine protected areas into a connected network — recognizing that fish stocks, currents and reefs ignore national borders. Lead with the ecological logic: protection only works at the scale ecosystems actually operate. The structural why is transboundary ocean governance as climate adaptation by small Pacific nations with little power but enormous marine territory. Fills the Oceania coverage gap noted in the audit.

stories.label: German ruling declares Google liable for false answers in AI Overviews
stories.summary: A German court ruled that Google's AI Overviews are Google's own speech — making the company legally liable for false statements its model generates. Lead with the precedent: this is the first major ruling to reject the 'it's just the algorithm' defense for generative-AI output. The structural why for the technically literate reader is liability theory — once an AI summary is the publisher's own words, the entire 'platform, not author' shield that protects search collapses for AI answers.

stories.label: Google's latest DiffusionGemma open AI model comes with a 4x speed boost
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's DiffusionGemma abandons the linear, token-by-token generation every mainstream LLM uses and instead produces whole blocks at once via diffusion — claiming a 4x speed boost. Lead with the architectural break: this is a different way to generate text, not a bigger version of the same thing. The structural why for the developer reader is that diffusion language models trade the autoregressive bottleneck for parallel decoding, and an open release lets anyone test whether the speedup holds.

stories.label: CISA to require federal agencies to patch some cyber vulnerabilities within 3 days
stories.summary: A new CISA directive compels federal agencies to patch certain vulnerabilities within three days — a sharp compression from the usual weeks-long timelines, phased in over 180 days. Lead with the number and what it demands operationally: three days to test and deploy across sprawling legacy systems is brutal. The structural why for the reader is the shrinking window between disclosure and exploitation — attackers now weaponize bugs in hours, so government patch cadence has to collapse to match.

stories.label: Man jailed due to faulty face recognition says Florida cops ignored other evidence
stories.summary: Robert Dillon was arrested on a child-luring charge after a facial-recognition system flagged him as a match — and he alleges Florida police buried exculpatory evidence to make the algorithmic hit stick. Lead with the named victim and the inversion: the tool meant to assist investigators became the case, and contradicting facts were ignored to protect it. The structural why is automation bias in policing — once software names a suspect, the burden quietly shifts to the accused to prove the machine wrong.

stories.label: Trump vows fresh Iran strikes after 'playing us for suckers'
stories.summary: Trump abandons the weeks-long claim that an Iran deal is 'close' and signals open-ended strikes, framing Tehran as having 'played us for suckers.' Lead with the collapse of the diplomatic track itself as the development — not a new strike, but the discarding of the off-ramp — and the mechanism that follows: an escalation with no stated endpoint pulls in every Gulf host of US bases. Affected are Iranian civilians and the Gulf states turned into front lines; power sits with a White House now committed to force over negotiation. Sentiment splits sharply between the Qatari and Indian wires (divergence 0.27) — let the reader weigh tone against fact.

stories.label: Anti-immigrant violence in UK 'shocking': UN
stories.summary: The UN rights chief calls the anti-immigrant unrest in Belfast and Southampton 'shocking' and singles out online incitement — Britain's media watchdog is now warning platforms that viral posts about a knife attack stoked the violence. Lead with the mechanism the reader should track: social-media amplification turning a single incident into coordinated street violence against immigrants (including Sudanese), and the state's choice to lean on platform regulation rather than confront the politics. Affected are migrant communities; accountability sits with both rioters and the platforms that monetise the outrage. Multi-source with the regional Turkish voice (TRT) alongside BBC and Al Jazeera.

stories.label: Middle East: UN chief warns of risk of 'full war'
stories.summary: Amnesty International labels the escalating displacement and settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank a 'state-led' ethnic-cleansing campaign — naming the actor (the Israeli government) and the victims (Palestinians, including Bedouin communities). Lead with the accountability finding itself: a major rights body putting a legal term to a deliberate state policy, while world attention is fixed on Iran. The structural why is that occupation is not a backdrop but an active, accelerating program of land control; continuation IS the development. Multi-source — Al-Monitor, Deutsche Welle, and the regional voice of Al Jazeera.

stories.label: Govt to merge bread subsidy into cash transfer program, cut 10 million beneficiaries from historic pillar of state support
stories.summary: Egypt is preparing to fold its century-old bread subsidy into the cash-transfer ration system and cut 10 million people from it — a Mada Masr scoop no wire is carrying. Lead with the number and what bread subsidy means in Egypt: it is the load-bearing pillar of social peace, the line whose removal has historically triggered unrest. The structural why is IMF-driven subsidy 'rationalisation' — moving from universal price support to targeted cash shifts risk onto the poorest and tests how much austerity the state can impose before the street answers. OIC accountability story with original regional sourcing; flag that figures come from officials briefing suppliers, not a public announcement.

stories.label: A Death in Detention Puts Tajikistan's Police on Trial
stories.summary: Six Dushanbe officers are being prosecuted over the death of Maksudjon Saidov in custody — but the charge sheet pointedly omits torture. Lead with that gap: a rare trial of police in an authoritarian state is real accountability, yet the careful avoidance of the word 'torture' shows how far the system will bend to acknowledge a death while shielding the practice that caused it. The structural why for the reader is how impunity survives even prosecution — by reclassifying the crime. A precedent-setting Central Asian story (OIC, fills the audit's Asia gap) from a specialist outlet; the feed offers no Tajik regional source to corroborate.

stories.label: How China's BYD saw its $1bn Turkey EV plant deal unravel
stories.summary: The $1bn BYD plant Erdogan unveiled in 2024 as Turkey's gateway to European EV production is an idle, grass-covered field in Manisa — and BYD is pivoting the investment to Hungary. Lead with the abandoned plot as the image, then the mechanism: Chinese carmakers chase tariff-free EU access and pick the host that offers the smoothest path, leaving Turkey with the announcement but not the factory. The structural why is how Global South industrial ambition collides with the cold logic of supply-chain siting. OIC story; merge the Gulf regional voice (Salaam Gateway) with Middle East Eye and the Yahoo/Reuters wire.

stories.label: Govt fuel levy drives cost-push inflation
stories.summary: A research paper finds Pakistan's own government is manufacturing inflation: the petroleum levy injects cost-push price pressure even as the State Bank raises rates to fight it — two arms of the state working against each other while households absorb both. Lead with that contradiction as the mechanism. The structural why for the reader is fiscal-monetary incoherence in an IMF-constrained economy: the levy is a revenue tool the budget can't give up, so the central bank's rate hikes only suppress investment and credit without curing the price rise the state itself is causing. OIC macro story with Dawn's regional sourcing; pairs with Friday's federal budget.

stories.label: What a Drug Bust Involving a MrBeast Winner Says About LatAm's Marijuana Trade
stories.summary: A private jet co-piloted by a MrBeast-challenge winner, seized in Paraguay with 250kg of premium marijuana aboard, is the hook for a real shift: high-value cannabis now flows south from North America into South America, reversing the historic trafficking direction. Lead with the reversal, not the influencer. The structural why for the reader is how legalisation in the US created a premium-product export the southern market now imports — drug economics restructured by policy, with the trafficking map redrawn accordingly. An InSight Crime investigation, the kind of systemic read no wire offers; balances coverage toward Latin America.

stories.label: An Early Step on the Long, Strange Road to Photosynthesis
stories.summary: An ancient cyanobacterial lineage is letting biologists reconstruct an early evolutionary stage of photosynthesis — the process that turns light into life and made an oxygen-rich Earth possible. Lead with the stakes the curious reader will grasp: this is reverse-engineering the single most consequential metabolic invention in the planet's history, one step at a time. The structural why is that understanding how the light-harvesting machinery assembled itself informs both origin-of-complex-life questions and synthetic efforts to engineer better carbon-fixing systems. Specialist science done well — exactly the Quanta register the reader expects.

stories.label: Bucking RFK Jr., OB-GYNs release vaccine guidance that conflicts with CDC
stories.summary: For the first time, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has issued its own maternal-vaccination guidance — explicitly diverging from a CDC reshaped by RFK Jr.'s anti-vaccine agenda. Lead with the institutional rupture: a professional medical body publicly breaking from the federal public-health authority is a rare, consequential act, an admission that doctors no longer trust the official line. The structural why for the reader is what happens when science governance is politicised — guidance fragments, and pregnant patients are left navigating competing official recommendations. Accountability meets medicine, from a reader-aligned source.

stories.label: Cops Keep Getting Arrested for Using Flock to Stalk People
stories.summary: More than a dozen US cases now show police using Flock's automated license-plate-reader network to illegally stalk people — ex-partners, private individuals. Lead with the pattern, not a single case: a mass-surveillance system sold to departments for public safety is being turned, repeatedly, into a personal stalking tool by the officers trusted with it. The structural why for the technically literate reader is that pervasive ALPR infrastructure has no meaningful access controls or audit teeth, so misuse is not an aberration but a predictable property of the system. A 404 Media privacy exposé — original accountability reporting no one else does.

stories.label: Cyberattack shuts down major Australian sugar mills, disrupting harvest
stories.summary: Australia's second-largest sugar producer has been knocked offline by a cyberattack mid-harvest, halting parts of its operations. Lead with the physical consequence: a digital intrusion is now disrupting a food-commodity harvest on a tight seasonal clock, where lost milling days mean spoiled cane and real economic loss. The structural why for the security-literate reader is the convergence of OT (operational-technology) systems and ransomware crews — agribusiness and food processors are soft, high-leverage targets precisely because downtime is so costly and their security maturity lags banks and telecoms. Names the sector-level risk, not just one company's bad week.

stories.label: Apple reveals new AI architecture built around Google Gemini models
stories.summary: Apple — the company that built its brand on doing everything in-house — is rearchitecting Apple Intelligence around Google's Gemini models. Lead with the strategic concession: the most vertically integrated firm in tech is outsourcing the core of its AI to a rival, an admission that it could not build a competitive frontier model in time. The structural why for the developer reader is the consolidation of the AI layer into a few foundation-model providers, with even Apple becoming a customer rather than a builder — and the privacy and dependency questions that follow from routing Siri's intelligence through Google. A flagship HN-surfaced story on where the AI stack is concentrating.
